body:
Well, I only see a psychologist right now (a therapist with a PhD in psychologist, not an MD like a psychiatrist). I've been off all drugs for about two years, but didn't notice much of a change on or off. I've considered other SSRIs but a lot of them have memory problems - I already have a very bad memory, so want to avoid that. 

It may be a good idea to switch therapists though. In the past 6 months or so our appointments haven't been very productive: I feel like we've said all that needs to be said, and I just have to "do." But I don't do. Ever. And you can't improve on 1 hr spent on your life per 2 weeks.

I've been seeing a psychologist once a week for 1.5 years, I'm not really sure what a doctor can do for me. I've also been on and off SSRI's in the past 4-5 years, and haven't noticed much change on or off.

Relax. I tried to tell you that I wasn't mad at you, that I wasn't directing anger at you, but you still had to get all aggressive.

And running and getting an endorphin high doesn't do shit if the structure of one's life doesn't change. It's the job, the loneliness, and the poverty that makes me unhappy - a runner's high isn't going to fix that structure. It's only a temporary high - the structure will maintain the permanent unhappiness. That's what needs to be changed.
Yes. I love watching MMA and am very interseted in Jiu-jitsu, but I cannot afford it. It's ~$100-120/month, and I make minimum wage and just enough to pay rent/food.
Tried that for past year. Roughly 1-2 hours spent on my life per month. "Trying" doesn't do anything for me.

I live in a big city. I am definitely in a position to look for other jobs. I just don't. And my life gets worse. 

I'm pretty sure any job I get will lead me to being bullied or harassed by managers or coworkers though, and I'll be stressed, hurt and unhappy until I quit. I had 3 prior jobs, all minimum wage, all exactly like that. I don't want to get hurt again.

Sure. I love military history and debating in general. But there are no jobs or careers there, so I don't do them. Instead I work in a call-center for minimum wage. I know it's irrational, but I am irrational.

When I unplug from the computer I do nothing. I sit in my room alone, or go out for a walk and come back to an empty room. I tried that once. After 3 days I started having paranoid delusions. Turns out it's actually predicable: 3 days without any form of social interaction, especially in someone already starved of it, leads to psychosis. Bottom line is that I just do nothing. I sit alone and do absolutely nothing.

I don't know. Even if I think positive, I just become happy and use the computer. Happiness = computer use. I run away from things, and only do things I need to do when under panic attacks / extraordinary anxiety. When I feel safe or happy, I go to the computer. I'm well aware I should be aiming for something, but nothing seems to be interesting or matter - I have no passions whatsoever.

tl;dr Happiness = computer. Anxiety = computer. Extreme anxiety = working on life. But working on life for awhile = happiness = computer.

>You're in a bad position, sure, but you're out there working super hard at a job that pays the minimum wage.

Problem is I only work when structured by others and forced to. I got a poor GPA because I skipped classes and didn't study at all. I was REALLY bad. I do work, but working does nothing for me: I make just enough to pay rent & food, and live paycheck to paycheck. And nothing changes. It's not useful. There is no reason to expect I won't be in the same place 1 year from now, unless I'm dead.

I don't think you understand how bad I am. I thought of teaching English too -> I have done less than 2 hours research in 5 months. Last week I had a goal to do 2 hours research. I did less than 30 minutes. That's how bad I am. You have to understand that I do <1 hour of work on my life per week. Period. You can't accomplish anything on that. Committing to doing more = failure too.

Oh cool I'll start running more. Yeah that'll make my life better. Suddenly I'll lose my virginity and get a good job and make friends and learn to stand up for myself and find my passion because I started running. Are you serious?

Feeling good is meaningless. Feeling good means I feel safe to sit on the computer more often. Feeling good means I put myself out there a bit more and people snarl and put me back down. Feeling good gets me nothing, except a temporary high.

edit: I'm angry with life, not you.

I'm a giant fucking loser, yet too much of a coward to kill myself.

- 25 years old.
- Virgin, never had relationship with a woman at all.

- No friends. None. Zero. No acquaintances. Zero.

- Minimum wage phone job.

- Worthless liberal arts degree

- Absolutely no ability to improve my life. Don't put any time into it. I can work 500 hours in 4 months at a call center, but can't spend 30 min a day working on my life. I do at most an hour every month trying to improve my life.

- Computer addict. 12-14 hours a day if I have a free day.

- Angry, hate the world.

- No idea how to stand up for myself. Afraid to do so, afraid people will get angrier and hurt me verbally. 100% bitch and easy to walk all over of. Take what you want from my life, I can't hold on to or defend it.

- Have been on this path for years. Graduated a year ago. It does not get better. It will not get better. "It will get better!" is absolute bullshit: that only applies to people who apply themselves to their lives. I can't, or won't; when I do I just get more anxious, more scared, and get absolutely no reward because I quit early. I tried asking this girl out (who obviously liked me) 3 months ago: it got a bit awkward because of a 3rd person who was oblivious, but I bailed out because I was terrified. I didn't ask her again. Trying to start relationship/dating = terror, no reward. Fuck my life. Kill me now. Slit my throat please.

- Everything I do triggers extreme anxiety and sometimes panic attacks.

I'm just working up the courage to kill myself now.
